title: The Chicago scene in the 1950s and Bill Russell's dances
summary: Bill Russell promoted dances; Jackson was peddling and the scene was poor.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: When they were giving those slow drag dances in the 1950s. Bill Russell was promoting dances in England. It was Bill who was doing it?

Yeah, Bill Russell. He did it for about six weeks or something like that. He wasn't trying to make money, he was just trying to, if he could get his money back. He was just an enthusiast, jazz enthusiast. But the crowds varied quite a bit.
You weren't doing much in the 50s at all.
In the 50s? Let's see. What was I doing in the 50s? I must have been pedaling, yeah. I was pedaling. You weren't playing? No, I wasn't doing much.
The scene in Chicago must have been pretty bad during the 50s. Oh yeah, yeah.
It was bad now. It's not too bad now.
